summary: Takapoto Airport serves the remote Takapoto Atoll in the Tuamotu Archipelago of French Polynesia, providing a vital air link for residents and visitors to this isolated coral atoll. The small regional airport connects the community to Tahiti and other islands in the chain, supporting both local life and ecotourism in the region. Its single runway and modest facilities reflect the low-volume traffic typical of French Polynesia's outer island airfields.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate flights to Takapoto Airport?
A: Air Tahiti is the primary carrier serving Takapoto, operating small twin-engine aircraft on routes connecting to Papeete (Tahiti) and occasionally other Tuamotu atolls.

Q: How long is the runway at Takapoto Airport?
A: The airport features a single paved runway suitable for small regional turboprop aircraft, consistent with the compact size needed to serve a small atoll population.

Q: Is Takapoto Airport open to international flights?
A: No, Takapoto is a domestic airport handling only inter-island flights within French Polynesia. International travelers must connect through Faa'a International Airport in Papeete.

Q: Are there any customs or immigration facilities?
A: There are no customs or immigration services at Takapoto; all international formalities are processed at Papeete upon arrival in French Polynesia.
transport_tips: There is no public bus service on Takapoto, so travelers should arrange accommodation pickup or a rental in advance before arrival. The airport is a short drive from the village, and most guesthouses offer transfers when you book. A car or bicycle rental is recommended for exploring the atoll, as taxi options are very limited.
local_tip: If you're visiting for the lagoon or pearl farming, ask your guesthouse about timing your trip with low tide to walk across exposed reef flats to nearby motu (small islets) — it's one of the most memorable experiences the atoll offers.
